# MedLit — technical and scientific product summary

Version: analysis contract 4.1.0
Last reviewed: 2026-09-10

MedLit retrieves lawful scientific metadata and open-access text, including bounded machine-readable PDF page text, HTML table structures, and a limited set of supplements. It sends the available article text directly from the user’s device to the user-selected AI provider, validates the returned JSON, matches generated quotations against the supplied text, validates evidence-linked PICO fields, fills every question in the selected transparent rubric, and derives confidence and risk-of-bias concern from visible evidence and assessability.

Supported provider choices are Anthropic Claude, OpenAI, and Google Gemini. The user supplies the key. Web keys are memory-only and clear on refresh or disconnect; native keys use encrypted device storage; keys are not synced to Firebase or saved with analyses. A no-key external ChatGPT packet handoff is also available. It does not sign users into MedLit with ChatGPT or provide API access via a ChatGPT subscription. Imported responses retain an unverified-model label and pass the same quotation matching.

Rubrics are concise MedLit question sets aligned with concepts from RoB 2 for randomized trials, ROBIS for systematic reviews, ROBINS-I for non-randomized studies, QUADAS-2 for diagnostic studies, JBI for cross-sectional studies, and CASP for qualitative studies. The product does not claim to reproduce, automate, or validate the official instruments.

Appraisal confidence describes source completeness, matched passage coverage, and domain assessability. It is not an accuracy, truth, quality, or clinical-validity score. Applicability remains not assessed. Abstract-only reports are capped at lower confidence and clearly limited. No matched evidence or no assessable domains means insufficient confidence, not low risk. Overview counts are application-derived; generated narrative and descriptive fields require independent source review.

When structured references include DOI identifiers, MedLit checks a bounded number through Crossref and inspects indexed update relationships for retraction or withdrawal notices. The report states how many references and identifiers were found and checked. This is not a comprehensive retraction or citation-integrity audit.

Workflow features include batch citation imports, saved libraries, comparison tables, correction history, guided appraisal, portable read-only snapshots, local saved PubMed searches, and manual update/retraction checks. Known limitations include PDF reading-order errors, unsupported scans/OCR, incomplete figure/equation/complex-table interpretation, bounded supplement ingestion, possible model errors, inability to reanalyze raw data, English-language emphasis, bounded reference checks, and the lack of a claimed expert-validation result. Outputs are AI-assisted decision support, not peer review or medical advice.
